verdict: Your software engineering internship and CampusBites project point toward a Software Engineer role. I'd hesitate because the internship lines leave the features and fixes unnamed. Which parts of the inventory application did you build?
write_up: You have a Computer Science and Engineering degree, an internship at Meridian Health Supply, and projects that point toward software engineering. It's common for an early-career resume to lean on duties and team routines, but that won't stand out in a pile: a recruiter needs to see the code and problems that were yours.

The Personal Finance Tracker line is a good model. It names the application, what it does, and the language and visualization library you used. Your objective doesn't add much to that story, and Education sits above your work experience.
Let's start with the first Meridian line and name an inventory feature you developed. Then add a concrete example to the tests and fixes. You can trim the soft skills list to make room for that work.

cards.line: Motivated and detail-oriented Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position where I can leverage my technical skills and passion for problem solving to contribute to a dynamic team.
cards.cannot_tell: This names the job you want, but the rest could describe many graduates. Lead with your internship and the technologies you used instead.
cards.example: Computer Science and Engineering graduate seeking a Software Engineer position, with experience developing an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot.
cards.question: Which part of your internship work do you most want a recruiter to see first?

cards.cannot_tell: You have work experience as well as a degree. Put Experience above Education so the internship reaches a recruiter sooner.
cards.question: Can you move Experience above Education?

cards.line: The resume doesn't describe what Meridian Health Supply does.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter may not know the organization. A short description, if accurate, can give the inventory application some context.
cards.question: How would you describe Meridian Health Supply's work in one short phrase?

cards.line: Responsible for developing features for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.cannot_tell: The application and tools are named, but the features aren't. One feature would show what you developed.
cards.example: Developed [feature] for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot.
cards.question: Which inventory feature did you develop?

cards.line: Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team
cards.cannot_tell: Meetings alone don't show what you contributed. Add your part in planning if it was substantial, or trim this line to make room for the features.
cards.example: Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team, contributing [planning contribution].
cards.question: What did you contribute to sprint planning?

cards.line: Wrote unit tests to improve code quality and reliability
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see that you wrote tests, but not what they covered or what you used to write them.
cards.example: Wrote unit tests for [feature or component] using [test tool].
cards.question: What did your unit tests cover, and what tool did you use?

cards.line: Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The teams and solutions are left unnamed. A feature and the people you gathered requirements from would make this work concrete.
cards.example: Collaborated with [teams] to gather requirements for [feature] and deliver [solution].
cards.question: Who did you work with, and what feature and solution did you help deliver?

cards.line: Fixed bugs and performed code reviews
cards.cannot_tell: Both are useful engineering work, but a recruiter can't tell what you fixed or reviewed. Pick an example of each.
cards.example: Fixed [bug] and performed code reviews for [work reviewed].
cards.question: What bug did you fix, and what kind of code did you review?

cards.line: Provided technical support to students and faculty for hardware and software issues
cards.cannot_tell: Students and faculty are clear, but the issues could cover a lot. Name an issue you handled and, if you know it, how many requests you supported.
cards.example: Provided technical support to students and faculty for [hardware or software issue], handling [number] requests [frequency].
cards.question: What issues did you handle, and how many requests did you support over a typical period?

cards.line: Resolved tickets in a timely manner and documented solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The tickets and documented solutions aren't described. One example would show the kind of problem you resolved.
cards.question: What's one issue you resolved and documented?

cards.line: Built a Python application to track expenses and visualize spending with matplotlib
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model: it pairs your action with a named application and its functions, without relying on a generic claim about your skills.

fit.why: Your objective names Software Engineer, and your internship and projects show web and application development.
fit.level: entry level, a software engineering internship and a Computer Science and Engineering degree
fit.note: Your React and Spring Boot internship work and full-stack capstone point toward application development. Put the parts you built at Meridian alongside the project work so both are easy to find.
